steps.title: Meet Text Classification
steps.text: This extension lets you teach the computer to sort text into groups you choose, like "happy" and "sad" messages. It can also judge text with ready-made models, and your project can speak and listen. Let's take a quick tour.

steps.title: Build your model
steps.text: This button opens the model editor. Make a class for each group, then add example phrases to each class. The model learns from your examples, so the more good examples you add, the better it gets.

steps.title: Save and load models
steps.text: Use this button to save your model to a file, or to load one you saved earlier or got from someone else.

steps.title: Does the text match a class?
steps.text: This block is true when your model decides the text belongs to the class you pick, and false otherwise. Use it inside "if" blocks.

steps.title: Which class is it?
steps.text: This block reports the name of the class your model thinks the text belongs to.

steps.title: How sure is the model?
steps.text: This block reports how confident your model is about its prediction for the text. A higher number means the model is more sure.

steps.title: Check text for harmful language
steps.text: This block uses a ready-made model, so you don't need to train anything. It reports how likely the text is to be toxic, insulting, threatening, profane, and more. Pick which kind from the menu.

steps.title: Is the text positive or negative?
steps.text: This block gives the text a score. Positive numbers mean positive text, negative numbers mean negative text, and 0 is neutral.

steps.title: Say it out loud
steps.text: This block speaks the text out loud. Try giving it the class your model predicts.

steps.title: Ask a question and listen
steps.text: This block says your question out loud, then listens through your microphone for a spoken answer. Your browser may ask for permission to use the microphone.

steps.title: What did it hear?
steps.text: This block reports what the microphone heard the last time you used “speak, then listen”, as text. Use it anywhere text fits: for example, as the text your model checks.

steps.title: Change the voice
steps.text: Choose a voice for the speak blocks: squeak, tenor, alto or giant.

steps.title: React to a loud sound
steps.text: This hat block starts its script when the microphone hears a sound louder than the number you set. A higher number needs a louder sound.

steps.title: Try it yourself!
steps.text: I've started a script for you, with “when green flag clicked”, “ask and wait” and an “if” block. First, open Edit Model and add two classes with a few example phrases each. Then drag “matches” into the “if”, put the “answer” block (from Sensing) in its text slot, and pick a class. Click the green flag and try answering!
